title: How to Confirm Phone Number Ownership with Lookup Identity Match
summary: Send details like name, address, or date of birth and the Identity Match API will tell you if they match a provided phone number. Reduce fraud and verify identities quickly.
body_markdown:
Time to read: - - - - - August 31, 2026 **Written by**[Kelley Robinson](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/authors/author.krobinson) Twilion **Reviewed by**[Dhruv Patel](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/authors/author.dhrpatel) Twilion --- Identity Match for phone numbers in the United States and Brazil doesn't require carrier registration and approval. Phone numbers from Canada, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Spain, and the United Kingdom require[additional carrier registration and approval](https://twlo.my.salesforce-sites.com/countrycarrier/SN_CarrierRegistration_VFP) . Learn more about the[carrier approval process here](https://help.twilio.com/articles/14968525856923-API-Onboarding-Guide-Verify-SNA-Lookup-Identity-Match-Lookup-SIM-Swap-and-More) . There's a lot you can learn from a phone number.[Lookup Identity Match](https://www.twilio.com/docs/lookup/v2-api/identity-match) uses phone numbers as an identity to provide a zero-knowledge match against authoritative data sources like mobile carrier records. This allows you to build real-time confirmation that you're interacting with a real person linked to the phone number provided. Use Identity Match to prevent fake accounts and improve trust with legitimate, unique users. Customers can use Identity Match at sign up, login, and even during account changes or checkout. Best of all, Identity Match happens seamlessly in the background, with lower costs and friction than alternatives like credit bureau and document verification used to satisfy[Anti-Money Laundering](https://www.finra.org/rules-guidance/key-topics/aml) (AML) rules. This blog post will show you how to use Twilio Lookup Identity Match to confirm phone number ownership and reduce sign up fraud. Here's a sneak peak at what the Identity Match request looks like. Learn more about[accepted parameters](https://www.twilio.com/docs/lookup/v2-api/identity-match#query-parameters) and[coverage](https://www.twilio.com/docs/lookup/v2-api/identity-match#coverage) in the documentation, plus[how to test different outcomes with our "magic numbers" and special parameters](https://www.twilio.com/docs/lookup/magic-numbers-for-lookup/testing-identity-match-with-magic-numbers) . Copy code ```text # use test credentials found here https://console.twilio.com/us1/account/keys-credentials/api-keys export TWILIO_TEST_CRED_ACCOUNT_SID=ACXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX export TWILIO_TEST_CRED_AUTH_TOKEN=your_auth_token curl -X GET "https://lookups.twilio.com/v2/PhoneNumbers/+12345678900\ ?Fields=identity_match\ &FirstName=John\ &LastName=Twilion\ &AddressLine1=123+Magic+St\ &City=Owl+City\ &State=CA\ &PostalCode=12345\ &AddressCountryCode=US\ &DateOfBirth=20080313\ &NationalId=123456789" \ -u $TWILIO_TEST_CRED_ACCOUNT_SID:$TWILIO_TEST_CRED_AUTH_TOKEN # returns: # { # ... # "identity_match": { # "address_country_match": "exact_match", # "address_lines_match": "exact_match", # "city_match": "exact_match", # "date_of_birth_match": "exact_match", # "error_code": null, # "error_message": null, # "first_name_match": "exact_match", # "last_name_match": "exact_match", # "national_id_match": "exact_match", # "postal_code_match": "exact_match", # "state_match": "exact_match", # "summary_score": 100 # }, # "national_format": "(234) 567-8900", # "phone_number": "+12345678900", # "valid": true, # ... # } ``` ## Programming Language Support This tutorial is geared towards JavaScript developers, but you can find other languages below: - [Python](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/developers/tutorials/product/confirm-phone-number-ownership-lookup-identity-match-python) - [PHP](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/developers/tutorials/product/confirm-phone-number-ownership-lookup-identity-match-php) ## Prerequisites To code along with this post you'll need: 1. A Twilio account.[Sign up](https://www.twilio.com/try-twilio) or[sign in](https://www.twilio.com/console) . 2. \[Outside US only\][Submit this form for Identity Match approval](https://twlo.my.salesforce-sites.com/countrycarrier/SN_CarrierRegistration_VFP) (takes[2-4 weeks](https://support.twilio.com/hc/en-us/articles/14968525856923-Onboarding-Request-For-Lookup-Identity-Match-Lookup-SIM-Swap-Verify-SNA-APIs) ) 3. [Twilio CLI](https://www.twilio.com/docs/twilio-cli/quickstart) (I'm using v5.5.0) 4. CLI[Serverless plugin](https://github.com/twilio-labs/serverless-toolkit/tree/main/packages/plugin-serverless) (run` twilio plugins:install @twilio-labs/plugin-serverless` ) ## Build the App This post uses the[international telephone input Code Exchange project](https://www.twilio.com/code-exchange/international-telephone-input) as a starting point, but you could use your own sign up form instead. The base project relies on the excellent[intl-tel-input](https://intl-tel-input.com/) plugin for collecting phone numbers in[E.164 format](https://www.twilio.com/docs/glossary/what-e164) . ### Step 1: Clone the starter template Start by cloning the example phone number input using the Twilio CLI: Copy code ```text twilio serverless:init identity-match --template=international-telephone-input && cd identity-match ``` Add your Auth Token in the created` .env` file within the *identity-match* folder. Test out the project by running` twilio serverless:start` , you should be able to open[http://localhost:3000/index](http://localhost:3000/index) and see a phone number input form. ### Step 2:Extend your sign up form with Identity Match Identity match needs information about the phone number owner to match against.[Parameters](https://www.twilio.com/docs/lookup/v2-api/identity-match#query-parameters) can be any combination of name, address, national ID or date of birth. This example is going to use first and last name, so you need to start by making sure your form has fields to collect those separately: Open *assets/index.html* and replace everything inside the`
` tags with: Copy code ```text
``` This adds a first name and last name input in addition to the phone number input. Further down in *index.html* in the script section, add the following code under` const data = …` to extract the name input values. Copy code ```text data.append("firstName", document.getElementById("firstName").value); data.append("lastName", document.getElementById("lastName").value); ``` Then head over to *functions/lookup.js* file to make use of the data and call the Lookup Identity Match API. The existing code already calls the basic Lookup API for formatting and validation, so you need to add the additional data parameters to tell the API to use the Identity Match package. Inside the` try` block but before` const client` , create a` data` object: Copy code ```text const data = { fields: "identity_match", firstName: event.firstName, lastName: event.lastName, }; ``` Then add` data` as a parameter to the the existing Lookup fetch like so: Copy code ```text const lookup = await client.lookups.v2 .phoneNumbers(event.phone) .fetch(data); ``` ### Step 3: Interpret the results of a Lookup Identity Match response After calling the Lookup API, you need to decide what to do with the[information in the response](https://www.twilio.com/docs/lookup/v2-api/identity-match#response-properties) . Here's what the identity match portion of a sample response looks like: Copy code ```text { "first_name_match": "exact_match", "last_name_match": "high_partial_match", "address_lines_match": "no_match", "city_match": "no_match", "state_match": "high_partial_match", "postal_code_match": "no_data_available", "address_country_match": "exact_match", "national_id_match": null, "date_of_birth_match": "exact_match", "summary_score": 90, "error_code": null, "error_message": null }, ``` Possible responses include` exact_match` ,` no_match` , and` no_data_available` . Name and address fields also support partial matches. Learn more about[match scores in the documentation](https://www.twilio.com/docs/lookup/v2-api/identity-match#match-scores) . The API will respond` null` if you don't provide an input to match on. This application is only looking at name matches and will consider the match a success if it's an exact match or high partial match (e.g. Kelly instead of Kelley – happens all the time). Back in *lookup.js,* replace` const success = …` with the following: Copy code ```text const fnm = lookup.identityMatch.firstNameMatch; const lnm = lookup.identityMatch.lastNameMatch; const success = lookup.valid && (fnm == "exact_match" || fnm == "high_partial_match") && (lnm == "exact_match" || lnm == "high_partial_match"); const respBody = { success, msg: `First name is ${fnm}. Last name is ${lnm}`, }; ``` Then replace the` .setBody` call inside the` if (success)` block with: Copy code ```text response.setBody(respBody); ``` Finally, make two small changes to display the response message in the *index.html* file. Replace the inside of the` if (json.success) {` block with: Copy code ```text info.style.display = ""; info.innerHTML = json.msg; ``` And since you're no longer only checking the phone number, update the error message line ( error.innerHTML ) in the` else` block a few lines below: Copy code ```text error.innerHTML = "Cannot register with the information provided. Please ensure you're using a phone number you own." ``` ## Run the Application Navigate back to your terminal, and restart the application with twilio serverless:start (enter CTRL + C first if it's still running). Now head back over to[http://localhost:3000/index](http://localhost:3000/index) and test it out! ### Next steps for identity verification Try out different combinations with both real data and the[test parameters](https://www.twilio.com/docs/lookup/magic-numbers-for-lookup/testing-identity-match-with-magic-numbers) to see the results. You can extend your application with other Lookup packages like[Line Type Intelligence](https://www.twilio.com/docs/lookup/v2-api/line-type-intelligence) ,[SIM swap detection](https://www.twilio.com/docs/lookup/lookup-sim-swap) and more. Check out our[documentation to learn more about what's possible with the Lookup API](https://www.twilio.com/docs/lookup/api) . Another way to prevent invalid phone numbers is to do[phone verification - we also have an API for that](https://www.twilio.com/docs/verify) ! I can't wait to see what you build and secure.
